note: How the F11 Map page's globe looks (src/ui/globe_view.gd). Each pin kind is a small silhouette icon (content/look/map_icons.json: a bunker, a mug, a stall...; or one of the drawn marks: ring, goal, you, planet, cruiser) in its role's colour ('roles', 'pins' below); 'system', 'planet' and 'cruiser' are the icons beside the places in the list (the star system's chart, each planet, the cruiser); 'ink' is the globe's own lines (null = the player's HUD colour). 'player' is you (a pulsing triangle that points the way you look); 'goal' is the waypoint's colour: the pin it is at flashes, and out where no pin is it shows as its own marker. 'owners' recolours a pin the locals hold (Territory): green, and yellow-green while their supplies there run short; round a held outpost a ring of radius ring_px drains as their hold runs down (ring_back_alpha the empty part). Issue #425: once the cruiser has fallen the Remnant's outposts get the ring too (in their own red), and remnant_short (orange) while they run short and you could resupply them. The cruisers' rows in the off-planet list and their badges on the system chart are coloured the same way by who holds them (issue #497; 'empty' once a cruiser is taken and nobody holds it); when it changes hands (checked every refresh_s seconds) the row flashes white for flash_s seconds, starting the next time the Map page is open. Under the grid the ball's own ground shows faintly ('terrain', GlobeTerrain + globe_ground.gdshader): its real heights baked at 'size' texels (latitude by longitude), tinted from 'low' to 'high' by height and 'rock' where the mesas stand, the slopes lifted 'relief' times and lit from the top left by 'shade' (fading out as a texel grows from fade_px[0] to fade_px[1] pixels on screen, zoomed in, where the light would show the texels); until the bake is done the ball is the plain 'sea'. 'terrain_types' lays a planet type's own tint over 'terrain' (a type with none uses its base's): grey rock on the asteroid, and on the lava moon 'rock' is the lava, the molten low ground. 'system' is the Map page's star system chart (src/ui/system_view.gd): 'space' behind it with 'stars' faint dots, each planet's orbit at 'orbit_alpha' in the ink, a planet never under 'min_px' across, lit from the top left by 'highlight', a ring flattened to 'ring_tilt', names in 'label' and the planet's kind under at 'kind_alpha'; issue #576: 'sun' is the chart's centre, a disc of radius_px in 'color' with a glow twice as wide at glow_alpha, and the planets near it orbit it. 'cruiser' is the Remnant cruiser's cutaway (src/ui/cruiser_map_view.gd): the real ship rendered from starboard, 'stretch' times taller than it is so its rooms can be clicked, on 'space' lit by 'ambient'; floors, ramps and furniture painted by 'finishes', the hull, walls, trim and glass drawn as light in 'ink' ('ghost': fill face on, rim edge on), the screens, reactor and engines glowing; the hull's silhouette traced over it at 'outline_alpha'. Names and what goes on the map: content/core/flow/map.json.

station.note: A sealed station's outline (GlobeMap.station_shapes): its domes, pit and tunnels in the ink colour, 'fill' and 'line' alpha, drawn once a dome is at least min_px across on screen.

roles.note: Issue: the map's icons are coloured by who or what a place is. hostile: the Remnant (their outposts, barracks while they hold them, a hostile camp); locals: what the locals hold; friendly: a friendly native camp; merchant: anyone who sells (stalls, traders, the ship dealer, the fence); droid: droid merchants and relays; maker: a market stall a player can make a keeper for ('Build an NPC') or one they made; service: the port, the cantina and its owner, homes; neutral: ruins, wrecks, domes, landing pads; race: speeder races; vehicle: your speeders; rock: mountains, spires and boulders.

pins.note: Each pin kind's icon ('shape': an icon in content/look/map_icons.json, or one of the drawn marks: ring, goal, you, planet, cruiser, star) and its 'role' (the colour, from 'roles'); a 'color' wins over the role's.

details.note: Zoomed in, a place opens into what is in it (GlobeMap.town_details, place_details): the town's and every location's buildings as their real footprints, filled flat from above, and its stops as icons with their names. A place's footprints show once it is at least 'show_px' across on screen, its stops (the town's, a ranch's stands) once it is 'stops_px' across (the port's pin hides then; a stop's icon is 'stop_scale' times a metre in pixels, kept within 'stop_px', so a market of stalls does not pile up), and the stops' names once a metre is 'label_px_per_m' pixels (names that would overlap one already drawn are left off; hover still names them). Footprint colours: 'by_look' (the box's look), else 'by_kind', else 'default'; the barracks' blocks are 'barracks' tinted by who holds them (the owners' locals green once the locals do), the cantina's 'cantina'. 'skip_kinds' and 'skip_looks' are left off (floors, lamps). The town wall is a line 'wall_px' wide in 'wall'. 'alpha' is how solid a footprint is.

terrain_marks.note: Mountains, spires and boulders on the map (GlobeMap.terrain_marks: DesertLandforms' own spots, so each sits on the rock you can walk to). A mountain shows from the start, sized by how wide it is on screen between 'mountain_px' [min, max]; spires once a metre is 'spire_px_per_m' pixels, boulders once it is 'boulder_px_per_m', drawn 'boulder_px' (by its size, up to twice that).
